translationRepairs: Yet this is not fortune for the present; there must be verification later. I dare not speak of it—please verify on another day what is verified."
Yet this is not fortune for the present; there must be verification later. I dare not speak of it—please let another day confirm what comes to pass."
請他日證其所驗 asks later confirmation of the prediction; the before phrase 'verify…what is verified' is awkward and obscures that sense, while the proposed wording restores it cleanly.
And wood's number is three—perhaps the omen will run its course within three reigns!"
And wood's number is three—perhaps the omen will run its course within three twelve-year periods!"
In this Jupiter/wood omen, 三紀 is three twelve-year calendrical periods, not reigns; 'three reigns' misreads 紀.
Moreover wood's number is three—perhaps the blessing manifests within three reign periods!"
Moreover wood's number is three—perhaps the blessing manifests within three twelve-year periods!"
Same misreading in the literal: 三紀 means three twelve-year periods, not 'reign periods'.

An edict said: "When kings found states and establish names to pass down through generations, they must make what is hard to know into teaching and choose what is easy to avoid for the people's convenience.

An edict said: "When kings found states and establish names to pass down through generations, they must turn what is hard to know into instruction and choose easy names for taboo avoidance so as to convenience the people.

從易避以便人 concerns choosing easy names to ease taboo avoidance; the before 'easy to avoid' is incomplete, but the proposal's bracketed alternatives are not finished English, so a complete revised literal is required.
When Heaven favored me I saw that the great mandate would not return to Tang; plans to prop up Han came to nothing, and the rites owed a fallen house were spent in vain.
When Heaven above lent its aid, I knew the great fortune would not flourish; plans to assist Han came to nothing, and the rites of serving Yin were spent in vain.
Chinese has 廣運之不興 and 事殷之禮; the before invents 'return to Tang' and replaces 事殷 with 'fallen house'. The after restores the classical wording without those insertions.
The old Eastern Capital becomes the Western Capital; Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished and Youzhou given a Youguo Army governor.
The old Eastern Capital becomes the Western Capital; Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished and Yongzhou given a Youguo Army governor.
Chinese 雍州 is Yongzhou; Youzhou is a different place-name and a clear mistranslation.
The former Eastern Capital is changed to the Western Capital, and Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished in favor of a Youzhou Youguo Army military governor.
The former Eastern Capital is changed to the Western Capital, and Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished in favor of a Yongzhou Youguo Army military governor.
Same error in the literal: 雍州 must be Yongzhou, not Youzhou.
Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei was made chief of the enfeoffment rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;
Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei was made chief of the investiture rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;
冊禮使 is the investiture/ceding-rites envoy for the abdication context, not land enfeoffment; 'investiture rites' is correct.
On a yi day Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.
Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.
Opening 乙 before the office is the appointment formula (以), not a bare sexagenary day-stem; removing 'On a yi day' is required.
On the day yi, Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was appointed to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.
Appointing Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.
Same appointment reading of 乙/以: the literal must not invent 'On the day yi' without a full binome.
the father, King Wenming, posthumous Emperor Wenmu, temple Liezu, fourth chamber, tomb Xianning; the mother, Grand Lady of Jin Wang, Empress Wenhui.
the father, King Wenming, posthumous Emperor Wenmu, temple Liezu, fourth chamber, tomb Xianning; the mother, Grand Lady of Jin, Lady Wang, Empress Wenhui.
晉國太夫人王氏 is Grand Lady of Jin plus Lady Wang; 'Grand Lady of Jin Wang' falsely fuses the title and surname.

〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the fifth month the Left and Right Changzhi became Dragon-Tiger Armies, the inner guards Forest of Plumes Armies, the sharp lancers and chargers Divine Martial Armies, and the personal horse guards Dragon-Prancing Armies.〉

〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the fourth month the Left and Right Changzhi became Dragon-Tiger Armies, the inner guards Forest of Plumes Armies, the sharp lancers and chargers Divine Martial Armies, and the personal horse guards Dragon-Prancing Armies.〉
Source note opens 四月; 'fifth month' is a numeral error.

〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the fifth month the Left and Right Changzhi were changed to Left and Right Dragon-Tiger Armies, the Left and Right Inner Palace to Left and Right Forest of Plumes Armies, the Left and Right Sharp Lances and Horse-chargers to Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, and the Left and Right Personal Followers and Horse Generals to Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies.〉

〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the fourth month the Left and Right Changzhi were changed to Left and Right Dragon-Tiger Armies, the Left and Right Inner Palace to Left and Right Forest of Plumes Armies, the Left and Right Sharp Lances and Horse-chargers to Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, and the Left and Right Personal Followers and Horse Generals to Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies.〉
Same date error in the literal: 四月 is the fourth month.

Zhang Quanyi, Prince of Wei and Henan Prefect concurrently military governor of Heyang, was advanced in enfeoffment; Qian Liu, military governor of the two Zhe circuits, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Wu and Yue.

Zhang Quanyi, Henan Prefect concurrently military governor of Heyang, was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei; Qian Liu, military governor of the two Zhe circuits, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Wu and Yue.
進封…張全義為魏王 newly advances him to Prince of Wei; the before wrongly treats Prince of Wei as an already-held title.
On xinmao the Emperor enfeoffed his brother Quanyu as Prince of Guang and his sons Youwen, Yougui, Youzhang, Youyong, and Youhui as Princes of Bo, E, Fu, He, and Jian.
On yiyou the Emperor enfeoffed his brother Quanyu as Prince of Guang and his sons Youwen, Yougui, Youzhang, Youyong, and Youhui as Princes of Bo, E, Fu, He, and Jian.
乙酉 is yiyou; xinmao is 辛卯 (a different day in the following unit).

On xinmao the Emperor's elder brother Quanyu was established as Prince of Guang, the imperial son Youwen as Prince of Bo, Yougui as Prince of E, Youzhang as Prince of Fu, Youyong as Prince of He, and Youhui as Prince of Jian.

On yiyou the Emperor's elder brother Quanyu was established as Prince of Guang, the imperial son Youwen as Prince of Bo, Yougui as Prince of E, Youzhang as Prince of Fu, Youyong as Prince of He, and Youhui as Prince of Jian.
Same sexagenary error in the literal: 乙酉 = yiyou, not xinmao.
On jiawu the old Eastern Capital residence became Jianchang Palace, and the Jianchang Court superintendent became palace superintendent.
On xinmao the old Eastern Capital residence became Jianchang Palace, and the Jianchang Court superintendent became palace superintendent.
辛卯 is xinmao; jiawu is 甲午 in the next unit.
On jiawu the former Eastern Capital residence was made Jianchang Palace, and the post of superintendent of Jianchang Court affairs was changed to superintendent of Jianchang Palace.
On xinmao the former Eastern Capital residence was made Jianchang Palace, and the post of superintendent of Jianchang Court affairs was changed to superintendent of Jianchang Palace.
Same correction in the literal: 辛卯 = xinmao.
On bingchen he held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue and feasted army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao downward, with graded gifts.〉
On bingshen he held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue and feasted army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao downward, with graded gifts.〉
丙申 is bingshen; bingchen would be 丙辰.
On bingchen the Emperor held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue, feasted and rewarded army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao down, bestowing goods in graded amounts.〉
On bingshen the Emperor held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue, feasted and rewarded army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao down, bestowing goods in graded amounts.〉
Same sexagenary correction in the literal: 丙申 = bingshen.
On bingchen in the seventh month Qu Hao, acting Jinghai staff officer and acting inspector, was recalled from mourning as Protector-General of Annan and full governor.
On bingshen in the seventh month Qu Hao, Jinghai Army campaign staff officer and acting residual governor, was recalled from mourning as Protector-General of Annan and full military governor.
丙申 is bingshen; 權知留後 is acting residual governor and 充節度使 full military governor—the before misrenders day and offices.
That month Xizhou reported that for two hundred li along the Yellow River from Daning to Gu Town the waters ran clear from the eighth of the month until the tenth, as before.
That month Xizhou reported that for two hundred li along the Yellow River from Daning to Gu Town the waters ran clear from the eighth of the month until the tenth month, as before.
至十月如故 means until the tenth month; collapsing 十月 to 'the tenth' wrongly reads a day.
Chief ministers asked that on the first palace entry each month and on Yanying audience days policy be heard—as a permanent rule.
Chief ministers asked that on the first of each month they enter the pavilion, and on the full-moon day hear government at Yanying Hall—as a permanent rule.
每月初入閣，望日延英聽政 has two schedule points: first-of-month pavilion entry and full-moon (望日) hearing at Yanying; the before drops 望日.

An edict posthumously honored the former military governor of Jingnan, Defender of the Secretariat and Prince of Shanggu Wang Zhou, as Grand Preceptor, and the former military governor of Wuchang, Concurrent Secretariat Director and Prince of Xiping Du Hong, as Grand Tutor.

An edict posthumously honored the former military governor of Jingnan, Defender of the Secretariat and Prince of Shanggu Zhou Rui, as Grand Preceptor, and the former military governor of Wuchang, Concurrent Secretariat Director and Prince of Xiping Du Hong, as Grand Tutor.
上谷王周汭 is Prince of Shanggu Zhou Rui; 王 is the princely title, not surname Wang, so 'Wang Zhou' is wrong.
Zhou of Jingnan, late Prince of Shanggu, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; Du Hong of Wuchang, late Prince of Xiping, Grand Tutor.
Zhou Rui of Jingnan, late Prince of Shanggu, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; Du Hong of Wuchang, late Prince of Xiping, Grand Tutor.
Chinese names 周汭; omitting the given name leaves the person underspecified beside Du Hong, who is fully named.
The Emperor judged the Yangzi too wide for timely aid; Jingzhou upstream had many warships and lay near Jiangxia—so he ordered Zhou Yu downriver by fleet.
The Emperor judged the Yangzi too wide for timely aid; Jingzhou upstream had many warships and lay near Jiangxia—so he ordered Zhou Rui downriver by fleet.
汭 is Rui; 'Zhou Yu' confuses a different historical name.

The Emperor judged that crossing the great Yangzi was hard to aid in time; moreover Jingzhou lay on the upper stream with many war vessels, very close to Jiangxia—hence he ordered Zhou Yu to raise a fleet and go downriver to rescue.

The Emperor judged that crossing the great Yangzi was hard to aid in time; moreover Jingzhou lay on the upper stream with many war vessels, very close to Jiangxia—hence he ordered Zhou Rui to raise a fleet and go downriver to rescue.
Same misreading of 汭 as Yu in the literal.
Yu's original surname violated the temple taboo of Emperor Wenmu; now because of the posthumous gift, since his line came from the Zhou of Wen, he was granted the surname Zhou.
Rui's original surname violated the temple taboo of Emperor Wenmu; now because of the posthumous gift, since his line came from King Wen of Zhou, he was granted the surname Zhou.
汭 is Rui, and 系出周文 is descent from King Wen of Zhou, not 'the Zhou of Wen'.
Yu marched east; at E's border Langzhou broke faith, struck empty Jiangling, and plundered it bare.
Rui marched east; at E's border Langzhou broke faith, struck empty Jiangling, and plundered it bare.
Subject 汭 must be Rui, not Yu.
Yu thereupon led troops east; just reaching the border of E, he met Langzhou breaking faith and rising in revolt, exploiting Jiangling's emptiness to raid and break it, plundering nearly all.
Rui thereupon led troops east; just reaching the border of E, he met Langzhou breaking faith and rising in revolt, exploiting Jiangling's emptiness to raid and break it, plundering nearly all.
Same Rui/Yu error in the literal for 汭.
His men thought only of home and would not fight; Huai raiders routed them; Yu drowned himself in grief.
His men thought only of home and would not fight; Huai raiders routed them; Rui drowned himself in grief.
汭…自投于江: the name is Rui, not Yu.

When Yu's soldiers learned of it, they all looked to their homes and had no will to fight; they were defeated by Huai bandits, officers and men scattered; Yu in rage and grief threw himself into the river.

When Rui's soldiers learned of it, they all looked to their homes and had no will to fight; they were defeated by Huai bandits, officers and men scattered; Rui in rage and grief threw himself into the river.
Both literal occurrences of Yu for 汭 must be Rui.
Yu's birth surname violated Emperor Wenmu's taboo; on posthumous honor, as his line came from King Wen of Zhou, he was granted the surname Zhou.
Rui's birth surname violated Emperor Wenmu's taboo; on posthumous honor, as his line came from King Wen of Zhou, he was granted the surname Zhou.
Opening 汭 in the idiomatic must be Rui.
After Yu's defeat Wuchang, besieged for years without relief, fell to Huai raiders who carried Hong away and killed him.
After Rui's defeat Wuchang, besieged for years without relief, fell to Huai raiders who carried Hong away and killed him.
及汭兵敗之後 requires Rui, not Yu.
After Yu's army was defeated, Wuchang, besieged for years with grain exhausted and relief not arriving, in the end was taken by Huai bandits, who carried Hong off to the Huai army and killed him.
After Rui's army was defeated, Wuchang, besieged for years with grain exhausted and relief not arriving, in the end was taken by Huai bandits, who carried Hong off to the Huai army and killed him.
Same Rui correction in the literal for 汭兵敗.
